skill.name: github
skill.description: Use GitHub CLI commands to manage repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, releases, keys, secrets, and configuration.
skill.summary: Operate GitHub workflows from the command line with practical gh CLI examples.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Static Ruby backtick findings are false positives caused by markdown code formatting and fenced bash examples. The SSH key finding is also a false positive because the cited file is a public key. The remaining concern is that several documented gh commands can modify shared GitHub state without explicit safety guidance.

remediation.issue: State-changing GitHub commands lack confirmation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings before merge, delete, workflow disable, secret deletion, repository creation, and public gist examples. Tell users to confirm repository, branch, permissions, and organizational policy before running them.

remediation.issue: Public SSH key example can be misread as sensitive key handling.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that only .pub public key files should be uploaded and private key files must never be shared or passed to gh ssh-key add.

static_findings.snippet: Use the `gh` CLI to interact with GitHub repositories and services.

semantic_findings.title: Shared GitHub State Changes Without Safety Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes examples for approving and merging pull requests, disabling workflows, deleting releases, and deleting secrets. These commands can affect shared repositories, but the guidance does not tell users to confirm authorization, repository target, or impact before running them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are real GitHub CLI operations that can modify shared project state. The issue is contextual safety guidance, not malicious code execution.

content.user_title: Manage GitHub from the Command Line
content.value_statement: GitHub work often spans issues, pull requests, releases, Actions, and repository settings. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical gh CLI commands for common GitHub workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows gh authentication commands for status checks, login, and token refresh.
Provides commands for repository cloning, creation, forking, viewing, and listing.
Covers issue and pull request listing, creation, review, merge, close, and checkout workflows.
Includes GitHub Actions commands for runs, logs, reruns, workflow listing, and manual dispatch.
Documents release, gist, search, API, label, project, key, secret, variable, extension, alias, and config commands.
limitations: It is a command reference and does not validate user permissions or repository policy.
Several examples can change shared GitHub state if run without review.
It assumes the GitHub CLI is installed and authenticated.
It does not provide error recovery steps for failed GitHub CLI commands.

use_cases.title: Triage repository work
use_cases.description: List issues, view pull requests, inspect checks, and search project activity from a terminal.

use_cases.title: Automate release tasks
use_cases.description: Create releases, generate notes, upload assets, and inspect release history with GitHub CLI commands.

use_cases.title: Manage CI workflows
use_cases.description: View GitHub Actions runs, read logs, rerun failed jobs, and trigger workflows with inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Check my GitHub login
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GitHub CLI skill to show me how to check whether gh is authenticated.

prompt_templates.title: Create a pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GitHub CLI skill to create a pull request from my current branch and include a concise title and body.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate failed CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GitHub CLI skill to list recent workflow runs, view a failed run, and show the log command.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a release workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GitHub CLI skill to outline a safe release process with commands for creating a release, generating notes, and uploading assets.

output_examples.input: How do I see open pull requests and their checks?
output: Run the pull request list command to find open PRs.
Then run the checks command for the PR number you want to inspect.

output_examples.input: How do I create a release from an existing tag?
output_examples.output: Use the release creation command with the tag name and generated notes option, then upload any required assets.

output_examples.input: How do I add a GitHub Actions secret?
output_examples.output: Use the secret set command and enter the secret value securely when prompted. Confirm the target repository before saving it.

best_practices: Confirm the active repository and branch before running state-changing commands.
Use read-only commands first to inspect issues, pull requests, releases, and workflow runs.
Follow team approval rules before merging pull requests, disabling workflows, or deleting resources.
anti_patterns: Do not run merge, delete, or workflow disable commands without confirming authorization.
Do not upload private SSH keys or secret files to GitHub.
Do not create public repositories or public gists with confidential information.

faq.question: Does this skill install GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: No. It assumes gh is already installed and available in the terminal.

faq.question: Can it authenticate to GitHub for me?
faq.answer: It shows authentication commands, but the user must complete any login or token approval steps.

faq.question: Does it support pull request reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes commands to approve, request changes, comment, checkout, and merge pull requests.

faq.question: Can these commands change production repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Some commands can merge code, delete resources, disable workflows, or change secrets. Review them before running.

faq.question: Does it handle GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers listing runs, viewing logs, watching runs, rerunning failed jobs, and manually running workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe to add SSH keys with this skill?
faq.answer: Only upload public key files with a .pub suffix. Never upload private SSH key files.
